name: @openidentityplatform/ui-commons
description: Open Identity Platform shared commons UI, published as an ES module build and an AMD build from a single AMD source
//license: DECIDED: the repository's own LICENSE.md is authoritative, so this is CDDL-1.1 and that file ships in the tarball. Both halves matter. (1) Version: this field said CDDL-1.0 while the repository root LICENSE.md is CDDL **1.1**; they cannot both govern the same files, and the repository-level licence wins over the per-file header boilerplate. (2) Text: the packed tarball carried a declared licence and nothing to read, because this directory has no LICENSE file and `files` listed none. build/npm-package.js now copies ../../LICENSE.md into the payload and asserts that its heading names the same version as this field, so the two cannot drift apart again silently — that drift is exactly what went unnoticed here. RESIDUAL, not fixed by this task: every source header in this module still says 'obtain a copy of the License at legal/CDDLv1.0.txt'. Reconciling those headers is a repository-wide edit across far more than commons/ui, so it is out of scope for a build change; it is recorded here rather than left to be rediscovered.
//private: Kept deliberately per design decision D18. Phase 1 distributes this package as a Maven-attached tarball produced by `npm pack`, which honours "private"; only `npm publish` refuses. Task 3.11 removes this, after the phase-1 gate in 3.8.
//version: Must equal ${project.version} in commons/ui/commons/pom.xml. Enforced by build/check-version.js, run by frontend-maven-plugin's `check-npm-version` execution at `initialize` (task 3.6): npm names the packed tarball from this field while build-helper-maven-plugin names the artifact it attaches from ${project.version}, so drift attaches a path that does not exist and fails at `install` with an unrelated message. The check is declared in the module pom, which merges after the parent's pluginManagement executions, so it runs just after `npm install` rather than before it - a drifted build therefore rewrites package-lock.json before failing. Accepted so that ui/mock, which has no such check to make, is not dragged in.
//exports: The AMD build under ./amd is deliberately NOT in the emitted "exports" map. RequireJS and r.js resolve a module id by concatenating baseUrl (or a `paths` prefix) with the id — they never read package.json, which was measured against requirejs 2.3.7 with a valid exports field present and ignored (NOTES-dual-build.md section 2, case A). An AMD consumer reaches ./amd through a narrow RequireJS `paths` entry pinned to org/forgerock/commons/ui/common, or by copying ./amd into its composition directory. See NPM-PACKAGE.md and the header of build/npm-package.js. The emitted package.json is written by that script; the "exports" map there covers the ES module build and the static ./www payload only.
//peerDependencies: The libraries commons' own modules declare as dependencies. They are peers, not dependencies, because the consuming product's RequireJS `paths` block is the single binding authority for every one of them — and for handlebars it deliberately binds a different file than this package's source expects. A nested second copy of jquery, lodash, backbone or react in a UI composed by flat overlay into one global namespace means two plugin registries and failing instanceof checks across the commons/product boundary, not a subtle version skew. Versions are what the source is written against, taken from commons/ui/LIBS-INVENTORY.md (task 3.1).
//peerDependencies-not-listed: Seven libraries the commons Maven zip ships in libs/ are absent here because no commons module imports them: backbone-relational, bootstrap, form2js, jquery.ba-dotimeout, js2form, requirejs and selectize. They belong to the consumer or to ui-user; declaring a peer range for code this package never references would constrain consumers for nothing. requirejs in particular is the loader itself, loaded by a <script> tag. See NPM-PACKAGE.md for where each still comes from.
//peerDependencies-lodash: `lodash` is the one peer that states TWO MAJORS rather than a single caret, and it is deliberate. It is also the ONLY one of these 18 peers that openam-ui-ria has in its npm tree at all; the other 17 reach it through Maven, so they cannot collide. HISTORY, because this range has now changed once: until task 8.3 it read `>=3.10.1`, because openam-ui-ria was two majors apart from itself — it shipped lodash 3.10.1 at runtime (from the commons.ui.libs zip, later a file vendored into src/main/js/libs/) while its own package.json pinned 4.18.1 as a build-toolchain devDependency, and LIBS-INVENTORY.md section 10 records that split. A bare `^3.10.1` made the packed tarball impossible to install into its only intended phase-1 consumer — measured, `npm install ./openidentityplatform-ui-commons-3.2.0-SNAPSHOT.tgz` into a tree holding lodash 4.18.1 fails ERESOLVE, which would have hard-failed task 3.7 — and `^3.10.1 || ^4.0.0` could not honestly be written yet, because the source still called APIs lodash 4 had removed. TASKS 8.1, 8.2 AND 8.3 HAVE NOW RUN: 8.1 and 8.2 replaced every such call site and 8.3 moved openam-ui-ria onto npm lodash 4.18.1 and deleted the vendored 3.10.1, so the split this note existed to describe is closed. The range is therefore now a REAL TWO-MAJOR COMPATIBILITY CLAIM rather than a placeholder: this package's source is written to behave identically under lodash 3.10.1 and lodash 4, and both are supported. `>=3.10.1` is gone because it also admitted lodash 5, which nothing has tested. THE CLAIM'S EVIDENCE, AND THE CORRECTION IT CARRIES: the scan found 91 call sites across both commons packages and openam-ui-ria, NOT the 25 this note used to assert — 46 on APIs lodash 4 removed outright and 44 on APIs lodash 4 still exports under the same name with DIFFERENT BEHAVIOUR (the deep-clone flag, a trailing thisArg, the predicate forms of pick/omit, the property shorthands), which is why 'the APIs lodash 4 removed' understated the job. Every replacement was verified by differential evaluation against both libraries on disk rather than reasoned about; see openam-ui-ria/NOTES-lodash-4.md sections 5 and 12.1. WHY THE LOWER BOUND STAYS AT 3.10.1 rather than moving to 4: openidm-ui and openig-ui still consume this package's source through the commons.ui:*:zip:www Maven channel and still bind lodash 3.10.1 in their own main.js, and this change neither builds nor tests them — the both-major claim above is what protects them, not this range, since Maven never reads peerDependencies. Do not solve a conflict here in the consumer with `--legacy-peer-deps`: that suppresses every peer check in the tree, not this one. `peerDependenciesMeta.optional` does not solve it either — measured; npm still reports an unresolvable `peerOptional` conflict when the package is present at a non-matching version. ui-user must state the IDENTICAL range or the conflict simply moves.
//peerDependencies-underscore: 24 commons modules (22 here, 2 in ui-user) declare a dependency on `underscore`, which is NOT a package dependency and is absent here on purpose. It is a logical name the product rebinds, and WHAT IT REBINDS TO CHANGED IN openam-ui-ria TASK 8.3: it used to map to lodash, and now maps to the real npm `underscore` (1.13.8, exact). DO NOT ALIAS THIS TO lodash 4. It was tried and measured against a deployed instance: backbone 1.1.2's History.loadUrl calls `_.any`, lodash 4 removed it, and the UI never leaves "Loading...". Nineteen names these modules and their backbone/backgrid peers rely on are absent from lodash 4. An ES module consumer must supply an alias to a library with underscore semantics — real underscore, or lodash 3.10.1, which is what openidm-ui and openig-ui still do (they map `underscore` → `lodash` AND bind lodash to the vendored 3.10.1 file, so both names land on one library there). Four modules that used to be in this count were rebound to `lodash` in 8.3 because they need APIs underscore lacks (`_.cloneDeep`, `_.curry`) or because they call `_.mixin` and their consumers are lodash-bound (UIUtils.js); every API those four use exists in both lodash majors, so they remain valid for openidm-ui and openig-ui. Same rebinding story for ThemeManager, NavigationFilter and config/AppConfiguration; NPM-PACKAGE.md lists all four. Not to be confused with the five ids that are merely spelled differently from their npm package — `placeholder` is jquery-placeholder and IS a peer below; those are renames a consumer aliases, not identifiers the product rebinds.
//devDependencies: The peer set is repeated here at the exact versions the source is written against, so that commons can resolve its own bare specifiers without a consumer present — the ES module build cannot be imported to verify it otherwise, and task 3.5's CI job runs the commons tests against both builds. Build-only entries: @buxlabs/amd-to-es6 generates the ES module tree from the AMD source, and @babel/* transpile the AMD tree (see build/npm-package.js).
//devDependencies-esm-tests: vitest, jsdom and sinon are task 3.5's. They run the ported commons suite in src/test/vitest against the EMITTED ES module tree under target/npm/esm — not against src/main/js — so a passing run is evidence about the build the package ships. The AMD build is exercised by the untouched QUnit files in src/test/qunit through commons/ui/mock, which is why both suites exist and why neither may be deleted in favour of the other; .github/workflows/ui-commons-dual-build.yml runs them in one job for that reason. `sinon` is pinned to 15.2.0 to match <sinon.version> in commons/ui/pom.xml, the version the QUnit run gets from the commons.ui.libs Maven artifact: the same test doubles on both sides, so a divergence between the two runs is about the builds and not about sinon. `jsdom` is 26.1.0 rather than the current 30.x because 30 requires Node >= 22.22.2 while frontend-maven-plugin pins Node 20.12.2 in commons/ui/pom.xml; 26.1.0 declares >= 18 and installs cleanly under both. `vitest` is 3.2.7 rather than 4.x for a related reason plus one of its own: 4.x makes `vite` a required peer that would have to be declared and pinned here as well, while 3.x carries it as a dependency.
